hypotheses.reasoning: catalog-svc's calls to the external translation API (api.translate.example) got slower first: 4.8s at 20:43:23, then 12s, then 30s timeouts starting 20:44:53. With no fail-fast, search-api's CatalogClient.getBatch calls also hit their 30s timeout on the same traces (t-1518, t-1522, t-1531). That held all 50 connections in search-api's pool to catalog-svc (50/50 in use, queue growing), led to checkout timeouts, and search-api returned 503s that web-bff passed on as GET /search 5xx. Nothing was deployed and the DB and cache show no errors. The TLS certificate warning is unrelated.
The underlying fault may be an outage or degradation at the third-party translation provider. Every failure is on the external POST to api.translate.example/v2/translate.
Pool saturation in search-api amplified the failure across all /search requests, but it is a downstream effect.

verdict.recommendedAction: Cut catalog-svc's translation API timeout sharply (for example to 2s) and add a circuit breaker that falls back to untranslated or cached text, so product batch requests don't wait on the external call. Check the translation provider's status and contact them. Lower search-api's CatalogClient timeout and isolate its pool (bulkhead) so a slow catalog-svc can't use up all 50 connections. Then drain or restart search-api's pool once translation calls are fast again.
